lines: Building small tools that do one thing exactly.
Turning messy ideas into systems that actually run.
Always building something I wish already existed.

about.name: Sam Rivera
paragraphs: I build developer tools and the odd piece of creative software — mostly around making a complicated thing legible before making it faster.
Away from the editor: film photography, long walks, and whatever I am curious about next.

principles: Human judgment stays in the loop.
Build the tool you keep wishing existed.

work.name: Plotter
work.why: A stream of measurements is not information until something shapes it. This reads a live feed and draws the one chart that answers the question you actually had.

work.name: TinyFS
work.why: Most filesystems are too large to learn from. This one is small enough to read in an afternoon and still correct enough to trust with real files.

work.name: Ledger
work.why: Plain-text accounting with no opinions about your money — it records what you tell it and refuses to guess the rest.

work.name: Signal Desk
work.why: Notifications arrive faster than anyone can read them. This collapses a day of them into the handful that changed something.

quote.text: A model can hold the context. It cannot hold the responsibility.

fortunes: The tool you keep meaning to build is the one you need most.
A system nobody can explain is a system nobody can fix.
Name it badly and you will build it badly.
Two hours of naming things saves two weeks of explaining them.
